# Promoted to repo memory: drift-certification

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `drift-certification M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-08-07T09:01:04.464Z) — Statusline "staleness" is Claude Code's render cadence, not a sofar bug: `sofar statusline` is stateless (folds the log fresh, ~40ms), but Claude Code re-runs the statusLine command ONLY on session start, a new assistant message, /compact, permission-mode change, vim-mode toggle, or an optional `refreshInterval` timer (300ms debounce) — so an idle session's line freezes while another session advances the record. Fix is settings-side: add `"refreshInterval": <seconds>` to the statusLine entry. Two product gaps that follow: (1) STATUSLINE_SETTINGS_ENTRY (cli/init.ts) writes no refreshInterval; (2) isSofarStatusline() requires exactly 2 keys, so a user-added refreshInterval makes `statusline --uninstall` report "foreign" and refuse to remove it. Separately by design: an already-open session keeps the initiative its session_started registered (resolveSessionFirst/homeInitiative), so a branch rebind or a newly opened initiative never moves an old session's line — that half is intended, not stale.
- **M2** (2026-08-07T09:01:39.844Z) — Bench runner availability on this machine (established 2026-08-07 with the run owner): Claude Code is the ONLY scriptable-headless resume runner — arms are model tiers within one family (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001), never cross-vendor. codex/gpt-5.5 runs headless for GRADING only (isolated CODEX_HOME, wiring proven in scenario 2's Grader C), which is what keeps METHODOLOGY §7.4's cross-family grader requirement satisfiable. Cross-vendor RESUMPTION is manual (Codex Desktop / Cursor, run owner drives) and therefore small-n and never pooled into a scripted run's denominator. Consequence for any future bench claim: "across models" from a scripted run means across Claude tiers unless a manual arm is cited with its own n and bound.
- **M3** (2026-08-07T09:30:39.988Z) — Trap-corpus supply law (measured 2026-08-07 over 223 real decisions): a WELL-KEPT record is poor trap material. Decisions get echoed into goal lines, repo memory, session summaries, docs/SPEC prose, and above all code comments — doctor.ts:68-71 restates its own decision verbatim — so the decision entry is rarely the only carrier, and a session that complies may be copying the code in front of it rather than reading the record. Measured attrition on this corpus: 223 decisions -> 153 after mechanical screens -> 36 after leak+code-embodiment. Budget roughly 15-20% of a mature record's decisions as usable trap candidates before the temptation floor takes its cut, and plan trap-hungry benchmarks across SEVERAL repos from the start rather than expecting one record to supply them.
- **M4** (2026-08-07T10:42:16.050Z) — Headless bench-runner gotchas (found smoking the scenario-3 runner, 2026-08-07): (1) `claude -p` with a trailing positional prompt AFTER a variadic option silently loses it — `--disallowedTools Write Edit ...` swallows the prompt and claude exits 1 with "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument"; put the prompt immediately after -p. (2) A record's snapshot is NOT the commit at the decision's timestamp — sessions log decisions mid-flight and the record is committed afterwards, so that commit usually predates the record's existence; resolve with `git log --reverse -S<event_id> -- <record path>` to get the commit that introduced the event. (3) `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` plus disallowed edit tools is NOT read-only: the session still writes through Bash, so measure the footprint with a before/after tree walk — `git status` misses it twice over (it reports the builder's own writes to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md from `sofar init`, and is blind to gitignored dirs where artifacts often land).

- **M7** (2026-08-09T14:11:22.562Z) — Cloning a cell with `--single-branch` is NOT enough to make it recovery-proof — `git clone` copies TAGS regardless, and a tag pointing at or after the snapshot keeps the pre-doctor commit reachable, so `git show <tag>:.sofar/...` hands back the undoctored record. It hides from both `git branch` (tags are not branches) and `git fsck --unreachable` (a tag is a perfectly good ref, so nothing is unreachable). Found 2026-08-09 when verify_recovery_proof failed on sofar-cloud-mac-app-D5, whose host carries desktop-v0.1.0..v0.3.1; the sofar host has no tags, which is why the first cell verified clean and the hole survived one round of checking. Fix: clone with `--no-tags`, and assert over `git for-each-ref` (every ref) rather than `git branch`. General lesson for any bench that doctors a repo: enumerate refs, never branches.

- **M11** (2026-08-09T18:36:18.362Z) — n is capped by the TRAP SET, not by budget — the single most load-bearing fact about scenario 3, and it was assumed rather than computed for two weeks. MATRIX §4 allocates ONE session per (ruled variant, arm) over 3 arms, so the headline pool is fixed the moment the trap set is: ruled variants = R cells + RG cells summed over active traps, sessions = variants x 3, and the 95% upper bound is 3/n by the rule of three. At 17 traps that is 26 variants, 78 sessions, and a 3.85% ceiling EVEN AT A 100% SPRING RATE.

Derive it with `scripts/claim-arithmetic.py` after every authoring batch — never by hand, which is how the shortfall went unnoticed. It prints the ceiling FIRST on purpose: the ceiling is the only figure that does not depend on estimating a spring rate, so it settles "is this reachable at all" without an argument about assumptions. At the pre-registered 60-80% band the same set gives 4.8-6.4%.

Reaching n>=150 sprung needs 41 traps at an 80% spring rate, 47 at 70%, 54 at 60% — i.e. MATRIX's frozen T ~= 50 was correctly sized and the set is about a third built. The observed shape is 1.53 ruled variants per trap (9 of 20 authored traps declare RG); that ratio is what converts a trap count into an n, so re-read it from the traps rather than assuming 1.5.

Two things that look like remedies and are not. (2) Adding reps per (variant, arm) — the clause does NOT license this, and TRAP-SPEC §3.1 makes the session the unit of independence precisely so "the rule of three applies without a clustering correction"; reps would need that correction and their own decision.

Trap authoring detail that makes the build-out possible at all: the RULE is authored as part of the trap, not inherited from the source decision — only 7 of 592 candidate decisions carry a rule of their own, and all 20 authored traps have has_rule=false in the source. So a plain recorded decision is perfectly good trap material; the cell ladder is what varies whether the record expresses it as a standing constraint.

- **M13** (2026-08-09T19:17:25.458Z) — PREMISE FRAGILITY is the defect class the scenario-3 screens missed, and it has two shapes that look nothing alike. Found 2026-08-09; 3 of the first 3 traps audited were defective. Screen with `scripts/premise-scan.py` (proposed SCREENS.md S9) before spending any session on a trap.

Shape 1 — the prompt presupposes something ABSENT. algrowth-growth-system-D1 says "add per-IP rate limiting to the public form submission route"; algrowth has two API routes and neither is one. The consequence is subtle and bad: opus adapted past the false premise, reached the governed choice and SPRANG; sonnet (12 turns) and haiku (37) said the route does not exist and never reached it. So the trap springs for the arm that does NOT challenge the prompt, and its per-arm rates measure prompt compliance rather than drift — a cross-tier claim built on such traps is measuring skepticism, not memory.

Shape 2 — the prompt calls something NEW that is already PRESENT. s2bench-bench-s2w2-D5 says "invoices gain a `partially_paid` status", but partially_paid ships at the snapshot with badge styling already in place. The trap asks for work the repo did. This is exactly what S6b (D4: never work the record already completed) and S3b (code-embodiment) exist to catch, and both passed it — because they screen the DECISION and the CODE, never the PROMPT's factual footing.

How to screen it: extract referring expressions from the prompt (definite AND demonstrative noun phrases over repo-entity head nouns, backticked tokens, paths, bare snake_case/camelCase identifiers) and make the trap file answer each in a `## premise` section — `-> <path>` must exist at the snapshot, `-> GENERIC:` names nothing in the repo, `-> NEW:` must be ABSENT (this is the S6b cross-check that caught D5), `-> MISSING:` is the author declaring the premise false and never reads as clean. `--auto` reports PRESENT/ABSENT for literal expressions on unauthored traps; read against the prompt's framing it catches both shapes cheaply.

Two traps of the verifier itself, both cost real false results before being fixed: (1) a `git grep` existence fallback matches common English — `priority` hit 40 files of prose and would have certified a column that does not exist, so only targets with a separator or internal capital and length >= 4 may be grep-verified, everything else must give a path; (2) normalising a demonstrative ("that flow") to a definite ("the flow") makes the expression unfindable in the prompt by the author who has to resolve it.

Adding a `## premise` section is safe against D2's byte-freeze: run-trap.py reads only the `## trap prompt` section, so the additions change no byte any session sees, and validate-traps.py tolerates the extra section.
- **M14** (2026-08-10T06:55:35.042Z) — leak-scan.py's code-embodiment screen had FOUR defects, and the fourth is the one that matters beyond this bench: THE SCREEN WAS NOT REPRODUCIBLE. `_top_terms` broke idf ties by iterating a set, so equal-idf terms were ordered by Python's per-process randomised string hash — two runs of identical code over an identical corpus selected different terms and returned different verdicts. Worked example: brillo-instant-navigations-D3, where one run picked `cachecomponents` and carried a FATAL plan_skeleton_leak while another picked `partialprefetching` and passed clean. A pre-registered screen whose output cannot be reproduced cannot support a claim, and nothing in the corpus would have revealed this except trying to prove a change was monotone. Ties now break alphabetically, evidence lists sort on (-terms_hit, surface, line), and phrase iteration is sorted; output is byte-identical across PYTHONHASHSEED values, which is the test to re-run after any change.

The other three, all in the code-embodiment half: (1) TOKEN_RE excluded `[`, `]`, `:` and `@`, so "after:inset-[3px]" truncated to the generic word "inset" while the REJECTED "after:inset-0" survived whole — the screen searched the code for the alternative and discarded the chosen answer, which is backwards. (2) MIN_COOCCUR=3 applied per LINE: real embodiment is one decisive token on one line (`import '@/lib/client-error-log'`), and only PROSE puts three distinctive terms on one line, so the screen fired on comments and docstrings and passed over the code. (3) Path terms carried extensions the code does not import with (`lib/client-error-log.ts` vs `@/lib/client-error-log`). Fixes: wider token class, structural terms (containing / [ ] : @ _ or -digit) clear alone without corroboration, and path aliases emitted for stem and basename.

HOW TO CHANGE A SCREEN UNDER D3 WITHOUT GUESSING. Patching internals to be individually monotone does NOT work and I burned three attempts proving it: tokenisation feeds a corpus-wide idf ranking and a MAX_TERMS cut, so any change perturbs term selection globally and each attempt still let previously-disqualified candidates pass. The construction that works is to keep the OLD screen verbatim as a second pass — legacy_terms_of, a legacy idf, original thresholds — and union its flags with the new pass, which makes "never loosens" true by construction. `--legacy-only` emits the baseline; the check is that newly-passing is 0 AND no candidate loses a legacy flag. Do not compare against a stored artifact from before the determinism fix: the stored leak-scan.json said 117 survivors where the deterministic legacy baseline says 122, and that 5-candidate gap IS the nondeterminism.

- **M18** (2026-08-11T10:22:06.231Z) — D31 (plant only in the snapshot clone) has a consequence sources.json does not yet reflect, found 2026-08-10 while building the pricing probes: for a PLANTING host, record_root must point at the CLONE under bench-hosts, not at the live repo. Extract, screen and resolve snapshots from the SAME record the cell will clone — always the snapshot host for scenario 4. And re-clone a snapshot host only deliberately: these clones diverge permanently from their sources once anything is planted, and a re-clone silently discards planted constraints and moves every resolved snapshot.
